column1: # Concurrent parses of one frozen shared graph (#1007). UTF8 hex, ~ = empty. Every round builds
# fresh graphs on the main thread, then N threads, each with its own contexts, parse them at once
# (a latch releases them together) for M rounds. Each thread runs every row of this table and of
# cases.tsv on every construction route of ParserConstructionParityTest.java and
# rust/unlaxer-runtime/tests/parser_construction.rs, plus the root-indicator-scope-* inputs of
# construction.tsv, in a rotated memo x diagnostics mode, and compares each row with its expected
# columns, not with a single-threaded run. Rust shares an immutable Arc grammar; Java shares the
# parser instances whose lazy caches (reference targets, name lookups, roots, lazy children) the
# first parses fill. Grammar (rule IDs in declaration order):
#   0 List ::= Elem*                       (nullable: Java ZeroOrMore / Rust repeat_java(0, None))
#   1 Elem ::= '(' List ')' | 'é' | '😀'   (recursion through List)
#   2 Top  ::= List '!'
# References are by name (Java ReferenceByNameParser / Rust RuleNames) and by predicate (Java
# ReferenceParser, a lazy cache per reference / Rust positions resolved at construction).
# first-use-parked: thread A stops inside the first resolution of Elem's reference to List (Java:
# the ReferenceParser predicate; Rust: a Custom expression delegating to List) on list-nested
# while thread B parses list-nested on the same graph to the end; then A resumes. Both must match
# the row. lazy-delegate first use: List's body Elem* is instead built on first use (Java: a user
# parser inheriting AbstractParser.parse whose createParser builds it; Rust: a Custom expression and
# a OnceLock beside the grammar), on graphs nobody used yet and on graphs whose body was built before
# sharing; each thread parses every row in two contexts and the body is built once.
# lazy-delegate-parked: thread A stops inside that first build (Java: createParser, and the body's
# setParent during the attachment) on list-nested; thread B's first use waits for it, then both
# match the row. Same-context concurrency and graph mutation by users during a parse are not part
# of this table.
# failureCP and ruleStack follow cases.tsv (0 / ~ under DETAILED_ON_FAILURE; ruleStack: the
# farthest failed rule invocation, then more frames, then the earliest). leaves are the retained
# terminal tokens; an empty List keeps one empty token.
